Position A, 8 September, WhatsApp GHL Dev: Ahmed reported the Full Smile workflows built and blocked on a single approval to make them live, and asked for that approval so he can enable them. That is what this card was drafted to deliver, as an update on Patient Workflows 12714615372.

Position B, 14 September, WhatsApp Full Smile Management: Dr Jamal Sahloul asked to strip the engagement down, saying the practice is building more infrastructure than it needs, that neither he nor Lily will use the attribution GoHighLevel provides, and that at 750 a month GoHighLevel is not worth it against Flex Dental at 264 which already integrates with Open Dental. Naz then wrote the scope back to the client for confirmation: pause Google LSA, Meta Ads and ALL GoHighLevel operations and workflows, continue Web and SEO, Google Business Profile and organic, at 500 a month. Lily backed pausing Google/LSA for a month. Jamal asked whether the Google number reverts to the main office line, and Adham asked for a written description of what the 500 covers before they commit. As of the end of 14 September the client had NOT yet approved, and Naz said he will only flag the teams to pause once he has approval.

The decision Naz needs to make: does Full Smile GoHighLevel work go live, or get withdrawn? Firing this card as drafted would tell Ahmed to enable GoHighLevel workflows for a client who asked the same week to stop paying for GoHighLevel. The five deliverables this card was going to post are not lost: they are already specified on Monday item 12714615372 in its 4 August update.

Two sibling cards are governed by the same decision and should be resolved with it, not separately: fullsmile-booked-showed-sync (Open Dental appointment value definition, the exact attribution Jamal said he will not use) and fullsmile-intake-speed-audit (intake measurement out of the GoHighLevel account).

Recorded honestly: find_pending_queue_match returned NO lexical match between the 14 September scope message and this card, because the conflict is semantic rather than textual. Raising it was a drafter judgment call under 19b's conflict rule, so it is reviewable as one. Priority raised to 1: nothing else on Full Smile GoHighLevel can move until this is settled, and the client is waiting on Adham's question. Monday's status column was not consulted.

items.title: Intake Speed Audit
items.note: Section 19 audit covered Full Smile groups on all four boards. Patient Workflows 12714615372 covers building the follow up automations but nothing measures the existing funnel, the Reports item 12175493646 and its subitems are per platform ad reporting rather than intake, and Budget Shift 12766744655 and the Meta Campaign Review 12906933112 are media decisions. Nothing owns the intake measurement, so drafted as a new CRM item. Routed to CRM rather than Web and SEO because the data lives in GoHighLevel pipelines and call logs, matching how the equivalent Maadi Law intake work was routed. Kept separate from fullsmile-booked-showed-sync per the merge counter rule. Section 19b returned no match.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. In his 8 September message to Full Smile, Sohib laid out the numbers the account is being judged on: Meta put 132 leads in front of the practice last month and 6 became patients. The practice paid for all 132, so his argument to the client was that closing the conversion gap is cheaper than adding budget. He then committed to the practice that he is auditing how fast those leads get called back and where they drop off, and said that is usually where most of the 132 goes. This item is that audit. It is a commitment already made to a client who is deciding whether to keep spending.
  • Deliverable one, measure speed to first contact. For every one of last month's Meta leads, pull the gap between lead creation and the first genuine outbound contact attempt, by call and by text separately. Post the median and, more importantly, the share contacted within five minutes, within one hour, on the same day, and never. The never bucket is the one that matters.
  • Deliverable two, find where they stop. Map the 132 through the pipeline stage by stage and post the count surviving each step: contacted, reached a human, appointment booked, appointment showed, became a patient. Six patients out of 132 means roughly 126 stopped somewhere specific, and the whole point of this is to name that step rather than describe the funnel generally.
  • Deliverable three, separate bad leads from bad follow up. Split the drop off into leads never contacted, leads contacted and unreachable, leads reached and not booked, and leads booked and no show. Those four have completely different fixes and only the first two are within Flow's control.
  • Deliverable four, one recommendation. Turn the finding into a single named change with an expected effect on monthly new patients. Sohib has already told the client the target is 9 percent conversion, roughly 21 patients a month on the same spend, bringing cost per patient from $411 down towards $293, so the recommendation has to be measured against that number and not a generic improvement.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency, all of this is in the GoHighLevel account already. Do not mix this with the Open Dental booked and showed integration on the Booked Showed Sync item, which is a build and will not land in time for this reply. Use whatever booking data exists today, even if imperfect, and say which parts are estimated. Findings feed the August Account Review reply, so post the numbers here rather than only summarising them to the client.
  • done = a written breakdown of last month's 132 Meta leads is posted on this item showing time to first contact, the survival count at each pipeline stage, the four way split of why leads dropped, and one named recommendation with its expected effect on monthly new patient count.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer

items.title: Purchase Value
items.note: Section 19 audit covered MedStation groups on all four boards. NextGen Patient ID Mapping 12978886451 on CRM is Done and its five synced fields are booking clinic, service category, appointment status, first visit date and Patient ID, none of which is a money field. Appointment Status Sync 13002597767 and Send To NextGen 13020662201 move appointment state, not value. GA4 Conversion Tracking 13021300803 on Web + SEO is web side conversion counting. Ads Reports 12471121477 and its Meta and Google subitems are platform spend reports. Nothing owns revenue on the record, so drafted as a new CRM item. Section 19b returned no match; the nearest queue card is medstation-weston-lead-attribution, which splits Weston leads by origin. That counts leads, this attaches money to sales, and per the merge counter rule they are different kinds of work rather than one deliverable, so kept separate.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. On 14 September Jonatan at MedStation asked whether revenue from repeat purchases can be traced back to the original acquisition source, so the account is judged on lifetime value and return rather than first conversion. Sohib confirmed the structure is already right: the source is stamped the first time a patient is seen and stays on the record permanently, and every later sale sits on that same contact as a new opportunity rather than a new contact.
  • What is missing, and it was promised to the client. Sohib told MedStation the same day that the one gap is pulling the purchase amount onto each sale, and that it goes into the team queue this week. Without a value on the record the cohort reports return patient counts and no money, which is not what was asked for.
  • Deliverable one, land the value. Write the purchase amount onto every sale or appointment the NextGen and Neuryn sync creates, on the existing contact record.
  • Deliverable two, prove the cohort report. Produce revenue by original acquisition source at 30, 90 and 180 days for one real cohort and post the figures here, so the reporting Jonatan described can be shown to work end to end.
  • Constraint. Source attribution already works and 84 wrongly stamped records were recently repaired on another account, so do not re-stamp contact source on any existing record while adding the value field.
